answeredReviewFindings: Important (review round 2): the note printed Legion's defaultResources numbers as this deployment's standing budgets, and the deployment had changed its ephemeral-storage limits twice before this head was written. Fixed at 19f4e15c0b23e94967996d926e6aefbb9d3c147d by attribution and dating rather than by swapping one table for another: the mechanism sentence now says each container is held to its own limit of local ephemeral storage and carries no figure; the section heading is '## What the limit charges'; the clamp paragraph says the cluster admits a container's limit equal to its request rather than 'its 1 GiB request', which is the machinery that makes the implementer's raise real; a new paragraph says every figure in the note is this pod's, that this pod predates both of the evening's changes so it carries 1 GiB for every role, dates and cites both changes, and tells a reader to read their own container's limits, naming what is readable from inside and what is not; the six memory values are labelled Legion's repository defaults; and the closing clause no longer asserts a smallest role. Threads PRRT_kwDORFy7ds6ul7TA and PRRT_kwDORFy7ds6ul7S8 answered and resolved.

One correction to the finding, carried in the thread reply: dispatch://INFRA-51/comment/a9f52454 is ephemeral storage, not memory. Read in full it records agent-infra #80 rebalancing every role's ephemeral request and limit after the tester began being evicted too, and its figures sum to 10Gi, the cluster's per-pod ephemeral ceiling. Memory was not changed that night — dispatch://INFRA-51/comment/12ce8e6b reads a live issue pod created after the evening's applies and finds exactly the six default values, recording that the deployment stack sets no memory at all. The note cites bf8035e7 and a9f52454 for the ephemeral changes and 12ce8e6b beside the memory defaults.

Not copied in: the ephemeral figures of the 22:50Z rebalance (512Mi, 1536Mi, 3Gi). The note dates and cites that change rather than reprinting numbers an operator can move again; grep for each returns 0.

trickyParts: A finding can be right about the defect and wrong about the record behind it. The review named a9f52454 as a memory change and the instruction repeated it; the comment is ephemeral storage, and the memory record is 12ce8e6b. Opening both before writing is what caught it — the same rule that has caught every defect in this note, applied to a correction rather than to a draft.

The dating paragraph is the part most likely to rot next: it names two applies on one evening. It is written so that a third change makes it incomplete rather than wrong, since it says 'at least twice' and tells the reader to read their own limits instead of trusting any figure here.
